articles.title: The King's Cart Stops at the Scale
articles.summary: A palace steward asks a bridge guard to overlook one overloaded cart, then needs the same gate opened for a genuine emergency.
articles.summaryZh: 王宫总管要求守桥人放过一辆超重货车，数月后，他却需要同一座桥为真正的紧急事件开门。
storyParagraphs: After winter floods loosened three stones in the old bridge, King Heman approved a weight limit. Every cart would stop on the iron scale, and the beam must remain below a painted red line. The order was posted in large letters because merchants had complained that palace wagons were waved through while theirs were searched. Captain Nuo, who ran the gate, received one copy bearing the royal seal. The rule slowed traffic, but cracks stopped widening. By spring even impatient carriers had learned to place their cargo sheet beside the scale weight.

On the morning of the river festival, the palace steward arrived with a bronze bell, musicians, and six carts of stone seats. The bell had to hang before noon or the king would open the celebration in silence. The first stone cart drove the beam a finger above the red line. The steward told Nuo to lift the barrier and promised to write an exception afterward. Letting one cart pass seemed cheaper than embarrassing the palace before a crowded quay. Nuo moved his hand toward the chain. Then a grain merchant, waiting behind the convoy with half his flour unloaded, laid his own cargo sheet on the scale and asked whether tomorrow's written limit would still mean what it meant today.

The steward ordered the merchant removed. Nuo knew refusal might cost him his post, yet the sealed copy gave no festival exception and no officer authority to invent one at the gate. He lowered the chain. The palace unloaded half the stone seats and made two journeys. The bell crossed safely, but it was still lying on straw when the king reached the quay. The opening began without its first toll; the steward lost his festival bonus, and Nuo spent the afternoon before an independent reviewer explaining why he had delayed the royal convoy.

Three months later, floodwater trapped families on the eastern bank. A rescue wagon carrying rope and a lifting frame also pushed the beam above the red line. This time the posted order contained an emergency clause: the fire captain could authorise one crossing, record the load and reason, and submit the bridge for inspection afterward. Nuo checked the signature and raised the chain. The wagon crossed. Two paving stones cracked and were repaired from the emergency fund. The rescue was permitted by a rule made before anyone knew whose wagon would need it, not by the urgency in one official's voice.

At the next festival, the steward divided the stone seats before leaving the palace. When his convoy reached the bridge, he handed Nuo six cargo sheets and waited while the iron beam rose. The old royal seal remained under glass beside the scale. Across its lower edge, the same red line continued without a gap.
storyParagraphsZh: 冬季洪水冲松旧桥三块石板后，赫曼国王批准了一条限重令：每辆车都要停上铁秤，秤杆不得越过漆出的红线。商人此前一直抱怨王宫车队挥手便过，自己的车却要卸货检查，所以命令被用大字贴在桥头。守桥队长诺安收到一份带王印的副本。规则让车队慢了一些，桥缝却不再继续张开。到了春天，再急的运货人也会把货单放到秤砣旁边。
河祭清晨，王宫总管带着铜钟、乐手和六车石座赶来。铜钟若不能在正午前挂好，国王便只能在寂静中宣布开幕。第一辆石车把秤杆压到红线上方一指。总管让诺安先抬栏杆，答应事后补写例外。放过一辆车，似乎比让王宫在满岸人群前难堪便宜。诺安的手刚碰到铁链，排在后面的粮商便把自家货单放上秤台。他为了守规矩已卸下一半面粉，只问了一句：“明天这条红线还算今天这条吗？”
总管命人赶走粮商。诺安知道拒绝可能丢掉职位，可带印命令没有节庆例外，也没授权任何人在桥头临时造一条。他放下铁链。王宫只得卸下一半石座，分两趟通过。铜钟安全过桥，国王抵达码头时却仍躺在稻草上，开幕没有第一声钟响。总管失去节庆奖金，诺安整个下午都在独立审理官面前说明自己为何耽误王车。
三个月后，洪水困住东岸几户人家。装着绳索和起吊架的救援车同样把秤杆压过红线。这次，公开命令中早有紧急条款：消防队长可批准一次通行，写明载重和理由，并在事后安排桥梁检查。诺安核对签名，抬起铁链。救援车过桥后，两块铺石出现裂缝，由紧急款修复。车辆获准，并非因为某位官员喊得更响，而是依据一条在无人知道谁会求助以前便写下的程序。
下一年河祭，总管在王宫里便把石座分装。车队来到桥头，他先递出六张货单，等诺安看着铁秤慢慢升起。旧王印仍压在秤旁的玻璃下，印纸下缘那道红线没有为任何一辆车断开。
explanationParagraphs: The rule of law requires public power to operate through accessible, prospective and generally applicable rules rather than personal command. Independent review, reasons, remedies and equal application help restrain arbitrariness. Emergency powers may still exist when their legal basis, scope, duration, records and later review are defined. This is a general institutional explanation, not advice for a particular dispute.
explanationParagraphsZh: 法治要求公共权力依照公开、可预见且普遍适用的规则行使，而非听凭个人命令。平等适用、说明理由、独立复核与有效救济可限制任意权力。紧急权限并非不可存在，但须明确依据、范围、期限、记录和事后审查。这里说明的是一般制度原理，不构成个案法律意见。

articles.title: The Sentence Beneath the First Bridge
articles.summary: A young judge relies on a five-word case index to clear his docket until a fireboat waits beneath a raised bridge.
articles.summaryZh: 年轻法官靠五字判例索引清理积案，直到一艘救火船被挡在吊桥下面。
storyParagraphs: Judge Yanning wanted the harbour docket cleared before the trade fair. A promotion depended on reducing the stack of undecided files, and his clerk had prepared index cards that reduced old judgments to a line each. One card read: 'The bridge opener pays.' It came from a case in which a private owner had raised a bridge without warning to collect a night-boat fee, sending a cart into the canal. The five words were easy to remember. Yanning kept the full page folded behind the card but rarely opened it.

A new claim arrived during fair week. Keeper Su had raised the same bridge after the fire bell sounded so a pump boat could reach a burning warehouse. A spice cart drove around the barrier and broke an axle against the rising gate. Its owner demanded compensation and placed the five-word card's copied sentence before Yanning. The hearing room was packed, twelve more files waited outside, and the material action looked identical: Su had opened the bridge; a cart had been damaged. Yanning announced that the old decision would govern and asked his clerk to calculate the loss.

Before the written order was sealed, another fire bell rang. The next bridge keeper, having heard the hearing, refused to lift his span until the road was completely empty and a magistrate signed an indemnity. The pump boat waited six minutes in the channel. Fire reached a roof beam that might otherwise have been soaked. No one could prove exactly which boards those minutes had cost, but the harbour captain brought Yanning a clock record and asked whether every rescue keeper must now choose between a fire and a debt.

Yanning cancelled the promotion supper and reopened the first file. The unfolded judgment was longer than the index card. Its decision depended on private gain, knowledge that travellers were crossing, and the absence of any warning. In Su's case the fire alarm, raised barrier and public rescue changed the facts that mattered. The earlier court had not declared that moving a bridge mechanically created liability in every setting. By midnight, sealing a revised order meant admitting that his quick announcement had treated a useful shorthand as the judgment itself.

The next morning Yanning explained the difference in open court. Su did not pay for the spice cart merely because he had raised the bridge. The bridge office still had to replace its low barrier, which witnesses showed was hard to see behind loaded wagons, and the cart owner's decision to drive around it remained relevant. The old case stayed in the books; Yanning did not erase it. He wrote why its necessary reasoning applied to one pattern of facts and not to this one. The delayed decision left six trade disputes unheard that week, and the promotion went to another judge.

When the clerk rebuilt the index, he kept the five words on the front. Beneath them he added three small lines: private fee, travellers present, no warning. The full judgment was no longer folded behind the card. A red thread passed through both pages so that pulling out the short sentence brought the longer one with it.
storyParagraphsZh: 燕宁法官想在商贸节前清完港口积案。他能否升职，取决于桌上未决卷宗能减少多少，书记员便把旧判决各缩成一张索引卡。其中一张只写五个字：“开桥者赔偿。”原案中，私人桥主为了收夜船费，在没有警告的情况下升桥，使一辆正在通过的马车落进水道。五个字很好记，完整判词折在卡片后面，燕宁很少展开。
商贸节那周来了一宗新案。守桥人苏达听见火警钟，为让水泵船赶去失火仓库而升桥。一辆香料车绕过拦杆，车轴撞上正在升起的桥门。车主要求赔偿，把抄来的五字判语放到燕宁面前。听证室挤满商人，门外还有十二份卷宗，而眼前动作确实相同：苏达开了桥，货车受了损。燕宁当庭说旧判决应当控制本案，让书记员计算损失。
书面命令尚未盖印，港口又响起火警。下一座桥的守桥人听说了庭审，不肯升桥，除非道路完全清空并由官员签字保证他不用赔。水泵船在水道里等了六分钟，火焰爬上一根原本可能及时浇湿的屋梁。没人能准确证明六分钟烧掉了哪几块木板，港务队长却把钟表记录带进法庭，问今后的救援者是否都要在火灾和债务之间选择。
燕宁取消升职晚宴，重新调出第一案。展开的判词远比索引卡长。旧案的裁断依赖几个关键事实：桥主为了私利，明知路上有人，仍不作警告。苏达案里，火警、拦杆和公共救援改变了重要条件。早先法院从未说，只要移动吊桥便必然对任何损失负责。到了午夜，若改写尚未盖印的命令，燕宁就得承认自己把便于查找的缩句当成了判决本身。
次日，燕宁在公开法庭说明两案为何不同。苏达不因升桥这个动作本身赔偿香料车；证人同时证明，装满货物的车很难看见低矮拦杆，桥务处仍须把它加高，车主绕行拦杆的选择也要保留在事实中。旧案没有被删除，燕宁逐项写清它解决过哪种事实组合，以及为何没有解决眼前情形。判决推迟使六宗贸易纠纷未能在当周开庭，升职也给了另一名法官。
书记员重做索引时，正面仍保留那五个字，下面却添了三行小字：私收费、有人通行、无警告。完整判词不再折进卡片背面，一根红线穿过两页。以后谁抽出短句，长页也会一起被带出来。
explanationParagraphs: Precedent guides later cases through earlier judicial decisions. Its weight depends on jurisdiction, court hierarchy, materially similar facts and the holding necessary to decide the earlier dispute; a memorable phrase is not automatically the binding rule. Courts may distinguish a case or, when authorised, overrule it with reasons. The details vary by legal system, so this is education rather than case-specific advice.
explanationParagraphsZh: 判例原则以较早司法决定指导后来案件，其分量取决于管辖、法院层级、关键事实是否相近，以及原案为解决争点所必需的核心裁断；醒目的摘句不等于完整规则。法院可区分重大事实不同的案件，也可由有权法院说明理由后推翻旧例。各法域做法有别，本段仅作知识说明。

articles.title: The Missing Sack of Grain
articles.summary: One sack disappears from the granary, and the manager orders the last worker to prove he did not take it.
articles.summaryZh: 仓库少了一袋粮，管事要求最后离开的人证明自己没有拿走它。
storyParagraphs: After the night shift, one sack of grain was missing from the public granary. The manager had promised to release sixty relief carts before noon; delay would leave three villages waiting and cost him his harvest bonus. Porter Zhou Qi had left last and wore a patched coat. The manager pointed to the empty place, then ordered Zhou to prove within three days that he had not stolen the sack or repay its value and lose his job.

Zhou could only say the sack was still there when he swept the aisle. No witness had stayed. The gate book, key register and count sheets were all locked in the manager's room, yet the manager treated every gap in Zhou's answer as another mark against him. Proving that he had never touched the sack had no clear boundary; the specific accusation, meanwhile, rested on poverty, a late departure and an empty patch of floor.

The reviewer first accepted the quick arrangement. Then a clerk noticed that the nightly count jumped from line eighty-nine to ninety-one. The rear-door key had also passed among three workers without separate signatures. The manager called both details untidy but irrelevant and warned that opening the records would stop the carts. If the reviewer waited, the granary would pay drivers and miss noon. If he did not, Zhou would carry a loss that the granary itself had not traced.

The reviewer sealed the loading yard and opened the record room. Drivers shouted outside while grain dust hung in the still air. The skipped line could be a copying error; the shared key left several possible users; a damp delivery slip showed that one late sack had been moved toward the relief bay. None proved where the missing grain had gone. Together they showed that the manager's first story was not the only one the records allowed.

The manager demanded that Zhou name the thief. The reviewer refused. Failure to establish the accusation did not prove every contrary story, but an unexplained loss could not be turned into evidence merely because someone had to bear it. Zhou returned to work, the inquiry remained open, and the carts left after dusk. The granary paid the waiting drivers. The reviewer lost the governor's promised commendation for fast decisions.

Two days later, workers found the sack behind a sealed partition in the third relief cart. A clerk had moved it during the rain, entered it on the missing line, then copied the next number over the wet ink. The discovery explained the loss. It did not make the earlier accusation reasonable after the fact; at the hearing, the manager still had to support the claim he wanted used to dismiss Zhou.

At the next count, the same empty space remained visible until replacement grain arrived. The manager added two signatures to the key and inventory sheets. On the old sheet, beside the skipped line, Zhou Qi's name had been pencilled in and rubbed out. The paper kept the grey hollow, but no one filled it again.
storyParagraphsZh: 夜班结束后，公仓少了一袋粮。管事答应中午前放出六十辆赈粮车；每迟一刻，三个村子就要多等，他也会失去秋收奖金。搬运工周启最后离开，身上又穿着补丁外套。管事指着地面的空位，命他三天内证明自己没有偷，否则照价赔偿并离职。
周启只能说，自己扫过通道时粮袋还在，却没有证人留下。守门簿、钥匙册和清点表全锁在管事屋里，管事却把他每个答不出的问题都记成一笔嫌疑。要证明自己从未碰过那袋粮，根本没有清楚边界；提出具体指控的人，手里只有贫穷、晚走和一块空地。
审理人起初接受了这个省事的安排，随后有书记发现夜间清单从八十九行直接跳到九十一行，后门钥匙也曾由三个人共用，没有分别签名。管事说这些只是潦草，催他别耽误发车。查记录，公仓就得赔车夫，还会错过正午；不查，周启就要承担公仓自己也没查清的损失。
审理人封住装货院，打开档案室。车夫在门外叫喊，静下来的仓里浮着细粮尘。缺行可能只是抄漏，共用钥匙留下几个可能使用者；一张被雨打湿的交接条又显示，夜里有一袋粮被挪向赈粮区。没有一项能单独说出去向，合在一起却足以说明，管事最先讲的并非记录容许的唯一经过。
管事要求周启说出谁才是贼。审理人没有照办：眼前指控未获支持，不等于所有相反说法都自动为真；粮袋仍失踪，也不能只因必须有人承担，就把未知当成处罚证据。周启回去工作，调查继续。粮车黄昏后才走，公仓赔了车夫，审理人也失去总督许给快审官员的表彰。
两天后，工人在第三辆赈粮车的封板后找到那只袋子。书记曾在雨中挪动它，把去向写在缺掉的一行，又用下一行数字盖过湿墨。后来发现解释了损失，却不能倒过来让先前的指控变得充分；在那次审理时，想开除周启的人仍须拿出能支持自己说法的材料。
补粮运到以前，公仓那块空位仍留着。管事给钥匙册和清点表都添了双人签名。旧表缺行旁曾用铅笔写过周启的名字，后来被擦掉，只剩一块灰白凹痕。此后再没人把空白填成他的名字。
explanationParagraphs: Burden of proof allocates who must establish a claim and how persuasive the evidence must be. It includes the burden of producing evidence and, in many settings, the burden of persuasion. Standards differ across criminal, civil and administrative proceedings and across jurisdictions. A failed case does not prove every contrary proposition; this account is educational and not legal advice.
explanationParagraphsZh: 举证责任决定由谁提出足以支持主张的证据，以及证据须达到何种说服程度，通常涉及提出证据与最终说服两层负担。刑事、民事、行政程序和不同法域采用的标准并不相同。一项主张未获证明，也不等于所有相反命题自动成立。此处仅说明一般原理，不构成法律建议。

articles.title: The Moths That Never Changed Colour
articles.summary: As the woods darken, pale moths become rarer, though a child never sees a single moth change colour.
articles.summaryZh: 树林变暗以后，浅色蛾越来越少，孩子却始终没看到任何一只蛾改变颜色。
storyParagraphs: Lichen once made the trees of Lin Town pale grey. Light moths nearly vanished against the trunks, while dark moths were easy for birds to find. A child helped the naturalist pin yearly specimens and wanted to win the school exhibition before the autumn kiln fair. The prize would also renew the naturalist's tiny field grant for another year. When soot from new furnaces blackened the bark, he announced that the pale moths would darken themselves to hide. It was a neat answer, and the teacher had already reserved him a blue ribbon.

For twelve days he kept one pale moth and one dark moth under a net beside a blackened trunk. Neither changed colour. He then marked and released equal numbers of both forms. In the sooty wood, sixty-two marked dark moths returned but only nineteen pale ones did. In a distant grove where lichen remained, the advantage reversed. Birds found the more visible form more often. The moths did not choose their colour after landing. What changed first was which already different individuals survived long enough to breed.

The next summer, the child's box still contained pale and dark moths, but the counts had shifted. Dark parents had left more descendants near the kilns, so dark moths formed a larger share there. Pale moths remained common in the lichen grove. He nearly displayed only the black-wood row: it made his first claim look correct and would keep the ribbon. Then a storm blew soot from the town trees, exposing small grey islands beneath several moths. The easy story split in two.

The child left his finished board at school and followed another generation instead. He returned the ribbon card and helped the naturalist repeat marked releases in both woods, so the field grant expired. The town later required the kilns to use a cleaner fuel, an expense that closed one furnace for a month. Lichen slowly returned. The colour that had left more descendants beside black bark no longer did so everywhere; neither form had climbed toward a permanent best state.

Three years late, the child carried his specimen box into the classroom. He opened it while autumn rain tapped the window, without touching the wings. The hinge clicked once. Every pinned moth kept the colour it had when caught. Under each row he placed the survival count, the kind of bark and the year. The blue ribbon lay folded beneath the first label. Nothing in the box had changed colour, yet the number of pale and dark wings changed from row to row.
storyParagraphsZh: 林镇树干原本覆着浅灰地衣，浅色蛾停上去几乎看不见，深色蛾却容易被鸟发现。一个孩子每年都帮自然观察员把标本钉进木盒，想赶在秋季窑炉节前赢得学校展览；得奖还能替观察员续上一年的小额野外经费。新窑冒出的黑烟把树皮一点点熏暗后，他断言浅色蛾会为了躲藏把自己变深。答案整齐，老师连蓝绶带都替他留好了。
他把一浅一深两只蛾罩在黑树旁，连续看了十二天，每天清晨贴着网眼查看，谁也没有变色。随后，他给等量的两种蛾点上不会伤翅的小记号，再放回树林。黑树区找回六十二只深色蛾，只找回十九只浅色蛾；远处仍有地衣的林中，优势恰好反转。鸟更常找到同树皮反差大的那一种。蛾并未落到树上才选择颜色，先改变的是哪些本来就不同的个体能活到繁殖。
第二年夏天，孩子的盒中仍有浅蛾和深蛾，数量却换了比例。黑树旁活下来的深色亲代留下更多后代，深色在那里增加；地衣林里仍是浅色占多。他差点只展出黑林一排，那会让原先说法看似正确，也能保住绶带。一场雨冲淡树皮烟灰，几只蛾腹下露出灰白小块，那个省事答案裂成了两半。
孩子把做好的展板留在教室，自己错过展期，又跟了一代。他退回绶带卡，同观察员在两片树林重新布点、标记和计数，野外经费也因此中断。后来镇上要求窑炉改用少烟燃料，一座窑因费用停工一个月；雨水冲过树干，地衣慢慢回来。先前在黑树旁留下更多后代的颜色，不再处处占优。两种蛾都没有朝一个永远最好的样子前进。
迟了三年，孩子才把标本盒带进课堂。秋雨敲着窗，他没有碰翅膀，只轻轻掀开盒盖，木铰链响了一声。每只针下的蛾都保持被捉到时的颜色；每排下面写着存活数、树皮和年份。那条蓝绶带折在第一张标签下。盒里没有一只蛾改变颜色，浅翅与深翅的多少却从一排换到下一排。
explanationParagraphs: Natural selection changes trait frequencies when individuals vary, some variation is heritable, and those variants differ in survival or reproduction in a given environment. Populations evolve across generations; individual organisms do not acquire a needed adaptation by intention. Selection is context-dependent, can involve trade-offs, and is not a ladder toward perfection. Resistance management aims to alter selection pressure rather than assume evolution stops.
explanationParagraphsZh: 自然选择发生在个体存在差异、部分差异可遗传，且这些变异在特定环境下造成生存或繁殖差别时。改变的是跨世代种群中特征的比例，并非个体因需要而主动获得适应。选择取决于环境，也可能伴随权衡，不会必然通向“更完美”。抗性管理是在改变选择压力，而不是让演化停止。

articles.title: The Greenhouse That Never Stood Still
articles.summary: A greenhouse temperature stays in a narrow range all day, so an apprentice assumes every window and valve should remain still.
articles.summaryZh: 温室里的温度整日保持在窄小范围，学徒因此误以为所有窗和阀门都不该再动。
storyParagraphs: The mountaintop greenhouse raised seedlings that feared both frost and heat. Apprentice Lin An watched its thermometer remain between two red marks through the week. He saw the old gardener open roof windows at noon, feed the stove at night, change the water valve and pull shade cloth whenever clouds moved. Because the number barely changed, Lin decided the gardener had finally found a perfect setting. A seed merchant promised him a bonus if two hundred trays were ready before the spring fair.

When the gardener left for one day, Lin tied the window handles, stove door and water valve at their dawn positions. No assistant could disturb them, and he would not waste time checking. The morning stayed cool; the thermometer sat neatly between the marks, and Lin signed the merchant's delivery note. At eleven the clouds broke. Sun struck the glass, damp soil steamed, and the needle climbed. The apparent stillness had depended on many small movements that Lin had just prevented.

He cut the cords and threw every roof window wide. The temperature fell, but slowly at first, so he also drenched the floor and shut the stove. Seedling leaves lifted for a moment. Then wind crossed the ridge, clouds returned, and the needle passed below the lower mark. Lin pulled the windows closed so hard that one latch broke. By dusk the stove was cold, several trays were waterlogged, and the most advanced tomato buds had begun to drop.

The merchant's cart arrived at dawn. Lin could hide the damaged trays behind healthy ones and keep the fair deadline. Instead, he refused the delivery, returned the deposit and lost the bonus that would have bought his winter boots. He spent the day moving trays by growth stage, repairing the latch and watching the needle. When it rose above the upper line, he opened a window one hand-width; as it returned, he narrowed the gap. At sunset he fed the stove before the stone floor lost all its heat.

The old gardener came back to find thirty-six dead seedlings laid beside the ledger. She did not give a speech. She set a young tray and a flowering plant under separate thermometers, then moved the shade over only one. Lin wrote the weather, plant stage, temperature and each response in four columns. Over the next month he adjusted earlier when clear sky approached and less sharply when wind was due. The useful range stayed narrow, but no single arrangement lasted from dawn to midnight or from new leaf to flower.

At the delayed spring fair, the merchant bought fewer trays and paid a lower price. Lin came home in patched boots. The greenhouse thermometer still moved between the same two red marks. When sunlight cleared the ridge, he looked at the young leaves, touched the warm glass and pushed the roof window open one finger-width. The broken latch, mended with dark wire, moved with it.
storyParagraphsZh: 山顶温室培育怕冷又怕热的幼苗。学徒林安看见温度表连续一周只在两条红线间移动：老园丁正午开顶窗，夜里添炉火，云一动又去调水阀、拉遮帘。数字几乎不变，林安便认定师傅终于找到一套完美位置。种商还答应，若两百盘苗赶上春市，就另给他奖金。
老园丁外出一天，林安把窗柄、炉门和水阀都绑在清晨位置，免得帮工碰乱，也省下反复查看的时间。上午凉爽，指针稳稳夹在红线间，他便签了交货单。十一点云层散开，阳光打上玻璃，湿土冒出热气，指针开始上爬。此前看似静止，恰恰靠许多小动作维持；他刚把那些动作全部拦住。
林安剪断绳子，把顶窗全推开。温度起初降得慢，他又浇湿地面、关死炉门，幼苗叶片一度抬起。山风随后越岭，云又遮日，指针越过下方红线。他猛拉窗柄，一只插销当场折断。黄昏时炉子已经冷透，几盘土泡了水，长得最早的番茄花苞开始掉落。
种商的车天亮便到了。林安原可把坏苗藏到健康苗后面，照期交货；他却挡住车，退回订金，春市奖金也随之没了，那笔钱本来要买冬靴。他把苗按生长阶段移开，修好插销，整天盯着指针。温度越过上线，他开一掌宽；指针回来，他便收窄。日落前，他在石地尚有余温时重新添火。
老园丁回来，看见账册旁排着三十六株死苗，没有讲道理。她把一盘新苗和一株开花植株放到两支温计下，只给其中一边拉遮帘。林安在本子上分四栏写天气、阶段、温度和动作。往后一个月，晴空将到时他提早调整，预报有风时便少动一些。适合范围仍窄，却没有一套位置能从早晨守到半夜，也不能从新叶一直守到开花。
迟开的春市上，种商少买了一批，价钱也压低。林安仍穿着补丁靴回家。温室温度表继续在两条红线间轻轻移动。太阳越过山脊时，他先看幼叶，再摸一摸发暖的玻璃，把顶窗推开一指。那只用黑铁丝补过的插销也跟着动了。
explanationParagraphs: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal variables within viable ranges despite changing conditions. Sensors, coordinating processes and effectors often form negative-feedback loops: a deviation triggers responses that oppose it, then those responses diminish as the variable returns. Stability therefore requires activity, not immobility. Set ranges and capacities vary, and failure or overcorrection can occur; the story is physiology education, not treatment guidance.
explanationParagraphsZh: 稳态是生物在环境变化下把内部变量调节在可生存范围内。感受、协调与效应环节常组成负反馈：偏离引发相反方向的反应，变量回到范围后反应减弱。因此稳定来自持续调节，并非静止不变。调节范围与能力会随个体和情境改变，也可能失效或过度；故事只作生理学说明，不提供处置建议。

articles.title: Good Seed in the Wrong Valley
articles.titleZh: 种在错误山谷里的好种子
articles.summary: The most productive wheat from Gold Valley is sent to Mist Valley and loses its first contest to an overlooked local seed.
articles.summaryZh: 金谷最丰产的麦种被送到雾谷后，第一次输给了原本不起眼的另一袋种子。
storyParagraphs: Gold Valley's farmers needed a wheat recommendation before the autumn seed fair. A five-village contract would keep the small trial station open through winter. The agricultural instructor planted the inherited Red-awn and Green-stem lines in alternating dry-valley plots. Red-awn yielded twenty-four baskets per plot; Green-stem yielded nineteen. She tied a gold 'best seed' label to the Red-awn sack. The result was real, repeated across Gold Valley, and financially difficult to ignore.

Farmers from damp, windy Mist Valley paid a premium for the winner. By midsummer, Red-awn stood tall and then lodged after three storms, producing only eight baskets per plot. A narrow strip of ordinary Green-stem stayed upright and produced fourteen. The instructor blamed planting depth and asked them to follow the Gold Valley instructions once more. One badly managed season seemed too weak to overturn orderly trials, so the gold label remained on every sack.

The next year she divided both lines between both valleys, matching sowing date, plot size and density. In dry Gold Valley, Red-awn again led, twenty-three baskets to eighteen. In Mist Valley, the order reversed, nine to fifteen. The inherited difference was not one fixed number that could be carried unchanged from one field to another. Wet wind did not turn Red-awn into Green-stem, nor did dry soil erase the difference between their seeds; it changed how that difference appeared in harvest.

Disease counts added another crack. Red-awn's taller, denser canopy retained moisture in Mist Valley and showed more leaf fungus; that disadvantage nearly vanished in the drier valley. An assistant suggested declaring Green-stem the true champion instead. The instructor shook her head and set the four harvest cards side by side. A new universal winner would repeat the old error: the gap could narrow, widen or reverse as growing conditions changed.

Five hundred gold labels had already been printed, and the guild opened in two days. The instructor pulled down the all-region notice, refunded Mist Valley's premium and lost one village order. With that order went the station's new threshing floor. She sold smaller paired lots instead: Red-awn for conditions like the tested dry fields, Green-stem for the tested damp, windy fields, each marked with a date and place rather than a promise about every farm.

Winter review cost another month. For every plot she recorded seed source, moisture, wind, soil and disease. She did not say inherited differences were unreal; the two lines repeatedly responded differently. She also refused to blame either valley as simply good or bad. The evidence belonged to particular combinations of seed and surroundings, and a new season or field still required a smaller trial before a broad recommendation.

At the next fair, four sacks stood on the instructor's table: Red-awn from Gold Valley, Red-awn from Mist Valley, Green-stem from Gold Valley and Green-stem from Mist Valley. She cut the old gold label into four strips and tied one beneath each yield card. No strip carried the words 'best everywhere'.
storyParagraphsZh: 金谷农会必须在秋季种展前给出一项麦种推荐，拿下五个村的合同，试验站才能撑过冬天。农师把可遗传的赤芒麦与青秆麦交替种进干谷小区。赤芒每区收二十四篮，青秆十九篮。她把“最佳麦种”的金标签系上赤芒种袋。结果真实，也在金谷多块田里重复过，站在账本前很难忽略。
潮湿多风的雾谷农人按高价买走冠军种。盛夏三场风雨过后，赤芒高秆大片倒伏，每区只收八篮；一条不起眼的青秆旧种却站得稳，收了十四篮。农师先把差距归给播种深度，要他们照金谷说明再试。一次管理不佳的收成看似不足以推翻整齐试验，金标签便继续留在每只袋上。
下一年，她把两种麦同时分到两座山谷，尽量配平播期、面积和密度。干燥金谷里，赤芒仍以二十三篮领先十八篮；雾谷的顺序却反转为九篮对十五篮。遗传差异不是一个能原封不动搬进任何田地的数字。湿风没有把赤芒变成青秆，干土也没抹掉种子差别；改变的是差别如何落在收成上。
病害记录又添了一道裂缝。赤芒较高密的冠层在雾谷留住湿气，叶部真菌更多；到了干燥金谷，这项劣势几乎消失。助手提议改称青秆才是真冠军，农师摇头，把四张产量卡并排铺开。换一个万能赢家，仍会重复旧错：环境一变，差距可能缩小、扩大，也可能反转。
五百张金标签已经印好，两天后行会开门。农师撤下“全地区最佳”的告示，退还雾谷溢价，也失去一个村的订单；试验站原定的新脱粒场随之取消。她改卖小份配对种包：赤芒标明适合已测试的干地，青秆标明在已测试湿风田更强，每袋都写日期与山谷，不再许诺所有农田。
冬季复核又花去一个月。她为每块地记录种源、水分、风、土壤与病害。两条品系反复作出不同反应，遗传差异并未消失；她也不再把某座山谷笼统说成好或坏。证据属于种子与周围条件的具体组合，新季节、新土地仍应先做小块试种。
下一次展会，农师桌上摆着四只袋：金谷赤芒、雾谷赤芒、金谷青秆、雾谷青秆。她把旧金标签剪成四条，分别系在产量卡下面。没有一条再写“处处最佳”。
explanationParagraphs: Gene–environment interaction occurs when the effect of genetic variation differs across environments, so trait differences may shrink, widen or reverse between settings. It is more specific than saying both genes and environment matter. Detecting it requires comparable genotypes across relevant conditions and adequate replication. It does not imply genetic effects are unreal or that every environmental change produces a different ranking.
explanationParagraphsZh: 基因与环境交互是指遗传差异的效应会随环境改变，因此品系间的表现差距可能缩小、扩大或反转。它比“遗传和环境都重要”更具体，通常需把可比较基因型置于相关条件中并充分重复。交互不表示遗传效应虚假，也不表示环境每变一次，排名必然反转。

articles.title: The Locksmith Who Always Left the Workshop
articles.titleZh: 每次都能离开作坊的锁匠
articles.summary: A locksmith rapidly joins two reluctant parts and still leaves empty-handed after every finished piece.
articles.summaryZh: 一名锁匠让两件难以扣合的零件迅速相接，完成后却总能空着手离开。
storyParagraphs: A riverside workshop had until dawn to make four hundred shipping rings for the last salt vessel. Its anchor chain rattled outside with each gust. If it missed the tide, the owner would lose the shipyard contract and six apprentices would go unpaid. Two kinds of metal clasp could join when heated and struck together, but only rarely; the floor already glittered with bent failures. The owner ordered a hotter furnace. More clasps collided, yet the copper softened and the catch still resisted. Then a locksmith arrived carrying one small grooved jig polished by years of use.

The jig held each pair in the needed orientation and pressed the stubborn catch along an easier route. Rings began falling into the finished basket every few breaths. The owner counted the sudden speed, promised the dawn shipment and stopped paying for extra hammermen. Each completed ring left the groove without taking the jig or locksmith with it; the same tool accepted another pair. By midnight, however, apprentices poured pieces onto the table faster than the locksmith could place them. Every groove was occupied. The queue grew even though the pile of raw clasps doubled.

A supplier then delivered a similar-looking clasp with a wider shoulder. It would not enter the groove. An apprentice forced one and scratched the jig; another let thick oil cover the catch, and production slowed. Hoping to recover the lost hour, the owner rolled the table nearer the furnace. Heat warped the jig's lip. Now even the proper clasp sat crooked, and three rings opened under a hanging weight. The short route had not changed which joining was possible, and it only worked while shape, temperature and contact remained suitable.

The tide bell sounded once. Loading the unchecked rings might preserve the berth, but a failed ring could drop a salt crate into the river. The owner shut the packing gate, paid the vessel's delay fee and returned the dismissed hammermen's wages. The locksmith cooled the jig, filed its lip and cleaned the groove. Apprentices separated the wrong clasps and tested each new ring under weight. Work resumed before sunrise, slower than the owner had promised but far faster than hammering alone. The contract survived; the tide bonus did not.

At noon the final crate went aboard. The owner found the locksmith washing black oil from his hands beside an empty table. Four hundred rings had left the shop, yet the grooved jig lay there ready for another pair. Its scratched lip was marked with the night's date. One failed ring still gaped beneath the hanging test weight. Before closing the gate, the owner moved the jig away from the furnace and placed one rejected wide clasp beside it.
storyParagraphsZh: 河城作坊必须在天亮前为最后一艘盐船做出四百只运输环，船的锚链正随阵风在门外哗啦作响。错过潮水，坊主就会丢掉船厂合同，六名学徒也领不到工钱。两种金属扣在高热和敲击下偶尔能接上，地面却已铺满弯掉的废件。坊主命人把炉火烧得更旺，碰撞虽多，铜件却先变软，卡口仍难越过。此时锁匠带来一只用了多年的小凹槽模具。
模具把两件扣子固定在合适方向，又把顽固卡口沿一条更省力的路压过去。成品每隔几次呼吸便落进筐里，坊主当场许诺按时交货，还辞去临时锤工。运输环离开后，锁匠和模具都没成为成品的一部分，同一凹槽还能接下一对。到了午夜，学徒倒上桌的零件越来越多，每只槽都被占着；原料堆加倍，队伍却只越排越长。
供应商又送来一批肩部略宽的新扣，外表相近，却进不了凹槽。一个学徒硬塞，刮伤模具；另一个让稠油盖住卡口，速度立刻下降。坊主为追回时间，把工作台推近炉边，热气又使模具边缘变形。合规格零件也开始歪斜，三只成环挂上砝码便弹开。这条捷径没有改变哪些扣合本来可行，也只有形状、温度和接触条件合适时才管用。
潮钟响了一声。未经检验便装船，或许能保住泊位，一只坏环却可能把整箱盐丢进河里。坊主关上装货门，支付误潮费，也补回被辞锤工的工资。锁匠让模具冷却，锉平边缘，洗净凹槽；学徒分开错件，每只新环都先挂重。日出前作坊重新出货，虽慢于承诺，仍比单靠敲击快得多。合同保住了，潮时奖金没有。
正午，最后一箱终于上船，船身还在潮水里轻晃。坊主在空桌旁找到锁匠，他正洗去手上黑油。四百只环已经离开，凹槽模具仍在桌面，第二天还能接下一对。被刮伤的边缘刻着昨夜日期，一只失败环还在悬挂砝码下张着口。关门前，坊主把模具移到远离炉火的位置，又在旁边放下那只被退回的宽扣。
explanationParagraphs: Enzymes accelerate reactions by binding substrates and lowering the activation free-energy barrier, often through orientation, microenvironment effects, bond strain or transition-state stabilisation. They are regenerated rather than consumed stoichiometrically and do not change reaction equilibrium. Rate depends on temperature, pH, substrate and enzyme concentration, inhibitors and cofactors; saturation and denaturation set important limits.
explanationParagraphsZh: 酶通过结合底物并降低活化自由能屏障来加快反应，常借助定向、微环境、键应变或稳定过渡态。酶在循环后可再用，并非按底物数量等量消耗，也不改变反应平衡。速率还受温度、酸碱度、酶与底物浓度、抑制剂和辅因子影响；位点饱和与蛋白质变性都是重要边界。

articles.title: The Long Band That Opened the Vault
articles.summary: A soft, apparently useless band reveals the shape that turns a vault only after it folds.
articles.summaryZh: 一条看似柔软无用的长带折叠以后，才露出能够转动金库的形状。
storyParagraphs: For the king's coronation, a vault maker promised a key no thief could recognise on sight. He linked many different small pieces into one soft band. Laid flat, it had no rigid teeth and looked useless. Under the right temperature and salt air, nearby sections bent while distant sections attracted or avoided one another. The band folded into a compact body, bringing three far-apart pieces together as a hollow surface that gripped the vault lock. Delivering it before the ceremony would pay the maker's winter debt.

One imported middle piece failed to arrive. The apprentice replaced it with a stiffer piece of the same weight and length, reasoning that the vault keeper would never count more than the number of links. The band still folded and fit the leather case, so he accepted the coronation bonus. At the first rehearsal, however, one corner bulged. The hollow met the lock unevenly and slipped when the keeper turned it. A change in one small section had altered contacts across the whole folded tool.

The apprentice pressed harder and warmed the lock. Heat loosened the band instead. After cooling, some sections returned, while others tangled with neighbouring bands into useless knots. The maker set one damaged band in a folding frame that kept the wrong parts apart until the intended contacts formed. The frame left afterward; it did not become part of the key. Two other bands remained clumped, showing that returning the room to its old temperature did not guarantee every altered chain would recover.

A repaired band opened the practice lock, then failed when held completely rigid in a clamp. Near the lock, its hollow had to shift slightly around the metal ridges. A partner pin on the vault door also helped align the first contact. The maker stopped drawing the key as one frozen outline. Its sequence constrained which shapes it could reach, while temperature, surrounding conditions, partners and small movements affected whether a working shape was occupied at the needed moment.

The palace clerk offered to accept the leather case unopened and preserve the ceremony. The apprentice instead returned the bonus, admitted the substitution and spent coronation morning rebuilding the band with the proper middle piece. The king used an older chest for the jewels. The workshop lost its royal display and sold two benches to pay the imported-piece debt. Before the rebuilt key left, the apprentice tested its fold, its movement at the lock and its recovery after a mild temperature change, not merely its length and weight.

A week later, the vault finally opened. The apprentice did not lift the band while it lay flat. He waited until the distant sections met, then pressed the hollow gently over the lock; the metal turned with a low click. In the empty leather case he kept the rejected stiff piece. It weighed exactly the same as the original and still bore the coronation seal.
storyParagraphsZh: 国王加冕前，金库匠人答应做一把窃贼看不出形状的钥匙。他把许多不同小节连成柔软长带，平放时既无硬齿，也毫无用处。在适合的温度与盐气里，邻近小节弯曲，远隔位置彼此吸引或避开，长带逐渐折紧；三处本来相距很远的小节靠到一起，形成抓住锁芯的凹面。若在典礼前交货，工坊就能还清冬债。
一节进口材料没有按时到。学徒用同样长、同样重的硬片替代，认定守库人最多只会清点节数。长带仍能折起，也装得进皮盒，他便领了典礼奖金。第一次试锁，转角却鼓出一块，凹面同锁芯贴不齐，一用力就滑脱。一处小改动，已经把整条折叠工具的接触关系带偏。
学徒加力，又把锁烤热，长带反而松开。冷却以后，有些小节自行归位，另一些却同旁边长带缠成死结。匠人把一条坏带放进折带架，暂时隔开不该相碰的部分，等原有位置重新靠拢；折带架随后离开，并不成为钥匙。另两条仍聚在一起，说明房间回到旧温度，也不保证每条改变过的带都能复原。
修好的长带能开练习锁，被夹具固定得完全僵硬后却又转不动。凹面接近锁芯时必须围着金属脊轻微移动，门上的伙伴销也帮助第一处接触对准。匠人不再把钥匙画成一张冻结轮廓。小节次序限制它能到达哪些形态，温度、周围条件、伙伴与细小活动又影响工作形态能否在需要时出现。
宫廷书记提出，皮盒不开封也可先验收，典礼便不会延误。学徒却退回奖金，承认换料，在加冕早晨重新装上正确中节；国王只得用旧箱盛放珠宝。工坊失去御前展示，还卖掉两张长凳支付进口料债。新钥匙出门前，学徒检验折叠、入锁时的活动和轻微温变后的恢复，不再只量长度与重量。
一周后，金库终于开启。学徒没有拿起平放的长带，而是等远隔小节相遇，再把凹面轻轻压上锁芯，金属低低响了一声。空皮盒里留着那节被退下的硬片。它和原件一样重，加冕印记也仍清楚。
explanationParagraphs: A protein's amino-acid sequence constrains how it folds into secondary, tertiary and sometimes multi-subunit structures. Shape, charge distribution, flexibility and interaction surfaces help determine function. Mutation, pH, temperature or chemical conditions can alter folding, dynamics or assembly; some changes are reversible and others cause aggregation or loss of activity. Equal protein mass therefore does not guarantee equal functional state.
explanationParagraphsZh: 蛋白质的氨基酸序列限制其形成二级、三级及有时的多亚基结构；形状、电荷分布、柔性和相互作用表面共同影响功能。突变、酸碱度、温度或化学条件可改变折叠、运动与组装，有些变化可逆，有些会聚集或失活。因此蛋白质量相同，不代表功能状态必然相同。

articles.title: The Bread That Stopped the First Mill
articles.titleZh: 让第一座磨坊停下的面包
articles.summary: The bread store is full while the first mill continues turning grain into flour no one needs.
articles.summaryZh: 面包仓已经堆满，河上第一座磨坊却仍在把谷物磨成无人需要的面粉。
storyParagraphs: Along the river, the first mill ground grain, a second workshop mixed flour into dough, and the final ovens baked bread. Each foreman was paid by how much material he pushed onward. After the harvest festival, sales fell, but the mill manager kept the waterwheel at full speed to win his monthly flour bonus. Bread already touched the store's highest shelf. Upstream, fresh sacks continued disappearing under the first millstone, and the next day's tally looked excellent.

By evening no more loaves would fit through the store door. Dough soured in barrels, flour covered the passage and mice reached a torn sack. The manager ordered the ovens hotter, gaining one aisle for an hour, but crusts burned while the first mill kept consuming grain. Stopping only the ovens merely moved the blockage backward. By midnight, intermediate rooms were full and the river wheel still turned, because nobody at the entrance could see the final shelf.

A millwright ran a float rod from the bread store to the grain gate. When loaves pressed the high mark, the rod pulled a catch at the first mill, narrowing the gate before more grain was committed to the bread line. The manager cut the cord after one trial, afraid of losing his flour bonus. The wheel surged again. Before dawn, two barrels split under sour dough, and flour dust clogged the second workshop's belt.

The manager fastened the rod back himself. As bread sold, the store level fell, the catch released and grain entered again. When shelves filled, the gate descended gradually rather than stopping every stone at once. The signal travelled quickly and reversed without rebuilding the mills. It acted near the first step that mostly sent grain toward bread, limiting wasted grain and crowded barrels before the final door jammed.

A pastry room opened later, drawing flour from the second workshop. On its first busy day, a full bread store closed the grain gate and left the pastry workers empty-handed. The millwright added a second measure for the branch and changed the linkage: bread alone could slow the bread-bound stream, but flour demand from pastries still opened enough supply. The manager learned that one end signal could not safely govern every branch as though they all made the same product.

The ruined festival batch remained on the books. The manager stopped the wheel for a day, surrendered his flour bonus and paid for spoiled dough, torn barrels and wasted grain. He also replaced foremen's separate output prizes with a shared measure of saleable goods and loss. The first week looked less productive because fewer sacks crossed the mill. The warehouse floor, however, stayed clear enough for one person to walk from grain to bread without stepping over waste.

At dusk, the last batch entered storage and touched the high mark. Far upriver, the first mill's water gate lowered with a wooden knock. The old cut cord still hung beside the manager's bonus ledger, its two ends joined by a dark knot.
storyParagraphsZh: 河边生产线从谷物开始：第一座磨坊磨面，第二间作坊和面，末端烤房做成面包。每处管事的奖金都按送往下一处的数量计算。收获节结束后，面包卖慢了，磨坊主管仍把水轮开满，想拿本月面粉奖金。成品已顶到仓库最高一层，上游新粮袋却继续消失在磨石下，日报数字十分漂亮。
傍晚，仓门再塞不进一条面包。面团在桶里发酸，面粉堵住通道，老鼠钻进破袋。主管命烤房加火，一小时内勉强腾出过道，面包外壳却焦了，第一座磨坊仍不停耗粮。只关烤房，阻塞不过向前挪。午夜时中间房全满，河轮还在转，因为入口没人看得见末端货架。
机匠从面包仓牵出一根浮杆，接回磨坊进粮闸。面包压到高线，杆便拉动卡口，让粮食尚未大批进入面包路径前先减速。主管试过一次，又怕奖金减少，把连杆割断，水轮立即恢复。天亮前，两只面桶被酸面撑裂，第二作坊的皮带也让面粉堵住。
主管亲手把浮杆重新接好。面包卖出，仓位下降，卡口松开，粮食再次进入；货架升高，闸门逐渐落下，并非一瞬封死每块磨石。信号来得快，也能自行解除，不必重建磨坊。它作用在谷物一旦越过便多半走向面包的早段，让浪费和拥塞在堵住仓门前就减下来。
后来第二作坊分出糕点房。开张第一天，面包仓一满，粮闸就关，糕点师却没有面粉可用。机匠又加一处支路量杆，改动连接：面包信号压低送往面包的部分，糕点订单仍能拉开足够供应。主管终于不再让一个末端信号把所有支路当成同一种产品。
节后坏账仍要支付。主管让水轮停了一天，放弃面粉奖金，赔掉酸面、裂桶与废粮，又把各处只奖励本段产量的办法改成共同记录可售成品和损失。第一周看起来磨得更少，因为经过磨石的粮袋下降了；仓库地面却终于能让一个人从粮堆走到面包架，不必跨过废物。
傍晚，最后一批面包入仓，碰到高线。远处第一座磨坊的水闸随即落下，发出一声木响。那截被割断的旧绳仍挂在主管奖金簿旁，两端用一个深色结重新接起。
explanationParagraphs: Feedback inhibition occurs when a pathway's end product reduces activity of an earlier enzyme, often the first committed step, commonly by binding a regulatory site. As product accumulates, pathway flux falls; when product is used or diluted, inhibition may ease. This rapidly limits waste and imbalance, but strength and architecture vary among pathways. Removing inhibition can raise production while creating new metabolic costs.
explanationParagraphsZh: 反馈抑制是代谢通路的终产物降低较早步骤酶活性，常作用于首个承诺步骤，并可通过结合调节位点实现。产物积累时通量下降，产物被消耗或稀释后抑制可减弱。这能快速限制浪费与失衡，但不同通路强度和结构各异；解除抑制虽可能增产，也会带来新的代谢代价。

articles.title: The Wasteland That Sent a Bill
articles.summary: A harbour leases its marsh as empty land, then pays separately for flood storage, cleaner water and young fish habitat.
articles.summaryZh: 港镇把湿地当作空地出租，随后又分别为蓄洪、净水和幼鱼生境支付代价。
storyParagraphs: Mayor Del needed warehouse leases before the council's winter budget. Beyond the harbour wall lay thirty hectares of reed marsh that paid no rent and looked empty at low tide. A trading company offered enough to keep the clinic and ferry operating if the town filled half the marsh, straightened its channels and built three sheds. Fisher Sula brought a woven mat of reed roots to the hearing and asked the council to count what happened there. Del counted only registered goods and wages. The lease was signed; stone fill created dry ground within four months, and eighty dock workers received pay.

The first autumn storm was not unusually high, yet water reached the fish market steps. Tide gauges showed the same peak as an earlier storm that the wider marsh had spread across shallow channels and vegetation. Now embankments sent more water toward the quay. The company said one flood could not be charged to its sheds, so Del bought larger pumps. They kept the market open during the next tide, but fuel, operators and maintenance consumed a third of the new lease revenue.

By spring, Sula's nets near the estuary held fewer juvenile mullet. Surveys found many young fish in the remaining creek edges and very few along the stone fill. Water leaving an upstream drainage ditch also carried more suspended sediment toward shellfish beds after part of the vegetated route had been cut off. The marsh had not produced invoices while it slowed water, trapped some material and provided sheltered nursery space. Removing different pieces did not create one identical loss; it exposed several functions whose replacements belonged to different budgets.

The ten-year lease lay open at the next hearing, with the buyback price written across its margin. Del signed beneath that larger number and ordered one embankment breached. Compensation cancelled a planned market roof, and dismantling a half-finished foundation wasted stone already paid for. Tidal flow returned to part of the site, while pumps remained necessary because restoration was incomplete and stronger storms still exceeded what the marsh could absorb. Fish counts improved over three seasons, not overnight. The clinic stayed open, but ferry fares rose when lease income fell.

At the next budget hearing, Sula laid the old reed-root mat across Del's ledger. Under it sat three separate papers: pump fuel, channel restoration and lost shellfish revenue. Del did not assign the marsh one magical price. He left the papers visible beside the warehouse lease before the council voted on the last dry parcel. Outside, new reed shoots had just crossed the ebb line.
storyParagraphsZh: 德尔镇长必须在冬季预算前拿到仓库租金。港墙外有三十公顷芦苇湿地，退潮时像一片不交租的空地。贸易公司答应，只要填掉一半湿地、拉直水道并建三座货棚，租金便足够维持诊所和渡船。渔民苏拉带来一张芦根编垫，请议会把湿地里发生的事也算进去。德尔只统计登记货物与工资，最终签下租约。四个月内，石料填出干地，八十名码头工人领到薪水。
第一场秋季风暴并不比往年特别高，水却漫到鱼市台阶。潮位记录显示，早先一次同等峰值曾被较宽的湿地分散进浅沟与植被，如今堤岸把更多水推向码头。公司说不能把一场洪水记到三座货棚名下，德尔便买来大泵。下一次涨潮时，泵保住了市场，燃料、操作员和维修费却吃掉新增租金的三分之一。
到了春天，苏拉在河口的网里很少再见幼鲻鱼。调查员在剩余溪沟边找到许多幼鱼，石填岸旁却近乎没有；上游排水沟流来的悬浮泥沙，在一段有植被的路径被截断后，也更容易抵达贝床。湿地过去减慢水流、截留部分物质、提供隐蔽育幼空间时不会开账单。不同部分被移除后，出现的也并非同一项损失，而是落进防洪、渔业和水质三本预算的不同后果。
下一次听证会上，十年租约摊在桌面，买回未开工地块的价钱横写在页边。德尔在那个更大的数字下签名，又命人拆开一道堤。赔偿金取消了原定鱼市顶棚，拆除半成品地基也浪费了已付钱的石料。潮水重新进入部分湿地，可修复并不完整，强风暴仍可能超过它能缓冲的程度，大泵也须保留。鱼类计数经过三个产季才有所回升。诊所没有关闭，渡船却因租金减少而涨价。
下一次预算听证，苏拉把旧芦根垫铺在德尔账本上。垫子下面压着三张纸：泵油费、沟道修复费、贝类损失。德尔没有给湿地写下一个万能价格，只让这些纸与仓库租约一起摊开，再请议会表决最后一块干地。窗外，新芦芽刚刚越过退潮线。
explanationParagraphs: Ecosystem services are benefits people obtain from ecological processes, including provisioning, regulating and cultural benefits and the supporting processes behind them. Wetlands may attenuate some floods, retain nutrients or sediment and provide nursery habitat, but effects depend on location, condition and event size. Valuation can reveal hidden trade-offs without implying every relationship has one market price or that engineered substitutes are equivalent.
explanationParagraphsZh: 生态系统服务指人们从生态过程获得的供给、调节、文化等收益及其支撑过程。湿地可能缓冲部分洪水、截留养分或泥沙，并提供育幼生境，但效果取决于位置、状态和事件强度。估值可揭示原本未入账的取舍，却不表示每种关系都有唯一市价，也不表示工程替代物完全等同。

articles.title: One More Sheep
articles.summary: Each household adds just one sheep to a common pasture, and no one can see how their own animal makes the grass disappear.
articles.summaryZh: 每户只往公共牧场多放一只羊，谁都看不出自己怎样让草消失。
storyParagraphs: River Village shared one pasture. In good years each of twelve households grazed ten sheep there. When lamb prices rose, herder Naro still owed twelve silver pieces on a winter roof. He added an eleventh ewe. Its wool and lamb would belong entirely to his family, while the grass it ate was one small part of what every flock used. One extra mouth could not bare a whole hill. Naro tied a red wooden tag around its neck and paid the first roof instalment.

Neighbours saw the ewe and made the same calculation. Within two weeks, nine households had added animals; some added three. At first every family sold more wool. No one wished to be the only household leaving grass for another's flock. By late summer, the measured grass height fell from a handspan to six fingers, and sheep returned hungry from the upper slope. Each family answered by sending animals out earlier and keeping them later, briefly protecting its own milk while giving roots less time to recover.

At the autumn meeting, the village head asked everyone to show restraint. All agreed because no number, season or first mover was named. The next dawn, the same flocks passed through the gate. After rain, bare patches washed into the ditch. Several owners removed neck tags before a count; admitting an extra sheep risked a private fine, while honest reporting would preserve grass for every household. Shared ownership was not the wound by itself. The old arrangement made added benefit easy to keep and damage difficult to assign.

When winter grass fell below three fingers, Naro led his eleventh ewe back from the gate and placed its red tag on the meeting table. The roof payment would now be late. The households marked who could use the pasture, set a seasonal total, rotated grazing areas and measured grass height together. Extra animals first brought a warning, then reduced the next season's share. Families short of fodder could borrow from a common stack and repay after lambing, so the poorest were not asked to carry the whole adjustment at once.

The first test came from the village head's brother, who drove three untagged sheep through the north gap at night. Turning them out meant a quarrel and cost Naro the man's wool business. Letting them stay would turn every red tag into decoration. The sheep were removed, the count entered publicly and the dispute heard before all twelve households. Spring grass recovered unevenly; a dry month still lowered it, and the villagers adjusted numbers rather than claiming their rules could command rain.

Naro paid for the roof one season late. Before spring grazing, every family brought its flock to the entrance board and wrote the number. The eleventh red tag had been cut in half: one piece hung from the pasture ledger, the other from Naro's barn door. When the last counted sheep passed, he lowered the wooden gate bar himself.
storyParagraphsZh: 河村有一片全村共用的牧场。草多的年份，十二户每家都放十只羊。羊羔涨价时，牧户纳罗还欠着修冬屋顶的十二枚银币，便多添一只母羊。羊毛与小羊全归自家，那一点草却只是所有羊吃掉的一小份。一张嘴不可能让整座山秃掉。他给第十一只羊系上红木牌，按时付了第一笔屋顶钱。
邻人看见那只羊，也照样计算。两周内九户都添了羊，有人一口气加三只。起初每家卖出的羊毛都增加，谁也不愿独自替别人留草。夏末，量过的草高从一掌降到六指，羊群从高坡回来仍在叫。各家便更早赶羊、更晚收栏，暂时保住自家奶量，草根却更没时间恢复。
秋季会上，村长请大家自觉少放。人人都点头，因为没有写数量、季节，也没人必须先动。第二天清晨，同样的羊群仍穿过门口。雨后，裸土被冲进沟里；还有人清点前摘掉羊牌，因为承认超量会带来私人罚款，诚实留下的草却由全村分享。伤口不只来自共有，而来自新增收益容易归己、损耗难以落到具体使用者的旧安排。
入冬草高跌到三指以下，纳罗把第十一只羊牵回门外，将红牌放上会议桌，屋顶欠款因此要晚一季。十二户划清谁能用牧场，订下季节总数，轮换地块，共同量草。超量先警告，再扣下一季份额；缺草料的家庭可从公堆借取，待产羔后归还，最穷的一户不必独自承受全部调整。
第一次考验来自村长的弟弟，他夜里从北侧缺口赶进三只无牌羊。赶走它们会撕裂会议，也让纳罗失去一桩羊毛买卖；放过，所有红牌就只剩装饰。三只羊最终被带走，数量公开入账，争执也在十二户面前复核。春草恢复得并不整齐，干旱仍会压低草量，村民只调整数量，不再说规则能命令降雨。
纳罗晚了一个产季才补好屋顶。春季放牧前，每户都把羊牵到入口木牌前，写下数目。那块第十一号红牌被切成两半，一半挂在牧场账簿，另一半钉在纳罗羊栏门上。最后一只已登记的羊通过后，他亲手落下门栓。
explanationParagraphs: A tragedy of the commons can arise when users receive much of the private benefit from added extraction while sharing depletion costs, making individually rational expansion collectively damaging. It is not inevitable and does not mean common ownership always fails. Clear boundaries, trusted information, locally fitted rules, monitoring, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution and support for unequal users can sustain many shared resources.
explanationParagraphsZh: 公地悲剧可能发生在使用者获得新增开采的大部分私人收益，却把资源耗损成本分摊给所有人时，个人理性的扩张便可能造成集体损害。它并非必然，也不表示共有资源注定失败。清楚边界、可信信息、在地规则、监测、分级制裁、争议解决及对不同处境的调整，都可能支持长期治理。

articles.title: The Summer the Lake Did Not Return
articles.titleZh: 湖没有回来的那个夏天
articles.summary: A lake repeatedly clears after nutrient pulses until one summer the same reduction in discharge no longer restores its former state.
articles.summaryZh: 一座湖多次在养分冲击后自行澄清，直到某年夏天，把排放降回旧水平也无法恢复原状。
storyParagraphs: Lake manager Iven had to keep the lakeside laundry works open through a weak trading year. Its treatment upgrade cost more than the town treasury held. Twice before, spring runoff had brought nutrients, algae had coloured the water green for a week, and the lake had cleared when flow subsided. Iven used those recoveries as evidence that the lake could absorb another season of permitted discharge. Each Monday he lowered a white clarity disk; at two metres he could still see it. The laundry kept sixty jobs, and the council postponed the upgrade.

The first summer bloom also faded after cooler weather. Submerged plants remained, small grazers fed on algae, and oxygenated bottom water kept much phosphorus bound in sediment. These processes helped the lake return after disturbance. Iven recorded the recovery but not how close the plant beds had come to their light limit. When the laundry requested a higher allowance during festival cloth orders, he approved it for six weeks. The extra income repaired the school roof.

This time the disk vanished at eighty centimetres, then forty. Dense algae blocked light; submerged plants thinned and stopped holding sediment. When algae died, decomposition consumed oxygen near the bottom. Under low-oxygen conditions, more phosphorus was released from sediment back into the water, supporting further growth. Wind stirred the now-unprotected mud. Several processes that had favoured clear water weakened together, while processes maintaining turbid water strengthened. Fish kills appeared along the sheltered bank after a hot night.

Iven cut the laundry discharge back to the earlier permitted level and expected the old recovery. The green water remained. Even after external input fell, stored nutrients and lost vegetation kept the lake in a different condition. Restoring the exact previous load was not the same as reversing the path by which the lake had changed. The point of transition could not be identified as one certain bucket or date; weather, sediments, food webs and spatial differences all affected it. By the time the disk disappeared, the safer warning margin had already been spent.

Winter was still weeks away when the laundry owners asked Iven for one last production season. He placed the white clarity disk on their wage ledger, then signed the closure and treatment order. Sixty workers received partial pay for eight weeks, financed by cancelling the new ferry pier; twelve left town. The council also restored shoreline plants, reduced other nutrient sources and monitored oxygen and sediment release. No single action promised a quick return. The first autumn storm produced another bloom even with the factory line closed.

The following spring, a few plant patches survived inside protective cages, and the disk became visible at ninety centimetres. That was improvement, not proof that the former clear state had returned. Managers kept two thresholds: one for mandatory load reduction and an earlier warning line that triggered investigation. They stopped treating past recovery as unlimited capacity to take the next disturbance. Uncertainty became a reason for margin rather than a number to round away.

Iven kept the white disk beside two water jars. The old jar was clear enough to read a date through; the newer one still held suspended green-brown particles. Before signing any discharge sheet, he lowered the disk from the pier and wrote the depth on the same tag that once said two metres.
storyParagraphsZh: 湖管员伊文必须让湖畔洗染厂撑过贸易低迷的一年，处理设备升级费超过镇库现款。此前两次，春季径流带来养分，藻类让湖水绿了一周，水量回落后又自行澄清。伊文把过去恢复当作湖还能承受一个排放季的证据。每周一，他从码头放下一只白色透明度圆盘，直到两米深仍能看见。洗染厂保住六十份工作，议会便推迟升级。
第一场夏季藻华也在天气转凉后退去。水下植物仍在，小型摄食者取食藻类，含氧底水又让不少磷留在沉积物中，这些过程帮助湖泊从扰动后返回。伊文记录了“恢复”，却没记植物床离光照下限有多近。节庆布料订单到来，工厂申请六周加量，他批准了。多出的收入修好了学校屋顶。
这一次，白盘先在八十厘米消失，随后只剩四十厘米。浓藻遮住光，水下植物变稀，固定泥沙的作用也减弱；藻体死亡后，分解过程消耗底层氧气，低氧条件又使更多磷从沉积物回到水中，继续支持藻类。风搅起失去植被保护的泥。几项原先有利于清水的过程一同减弱，维持浑水的过程却彼此加强。一个闷热夜晚后，背风岸出现死鱼。
伊文把工厂排放降回早先许可水平，以为湖水会照旧恢复，绿色却没有退去。即使外部输入减少，已经储存的养分和消失的植物仍把湖留在另一种状态。把负荷降到旧数值，并不等于倒走先前变化的道路。转折点也无法精确指认成某一桶水或某一天；天气、沉积物、食物关系与湖区差异都会影响它。等白盘消失时，较安全的预警余量早已用完。
离冬天还有几周，洗染厂主请求再做最后一个生产季。伊文把白圆盘压在他们的工资账上，随后签下停产与建设处理设施的命令。六十名工人领取八周部分工资，资金来自取消新渡船码头；十二人仍离开了镇子。议会还恢复岸边植物、削减其他养分来源，并监测底层氧气和磷释放。没有一项措施保证迅速见效。即使工厂线已经关闭，秋季第一场风暴仍带来一次藻华。
次年春天，保护笼内有几片植物活了下来，白盘在九十厘米处重新可见。这是改善，却不足以证明旧清水状态已经回来。管理者设下两条线：超过一条必须减载，更早的一条则启动调查。他们不再把过去能够恢复，当成承受下一次扰动的无限额度。无法精确预测的部分，被留成余量，没有再从表格里四舍五入掉。
伊文把白圆盘放在两只水样瓶旁。旧瓶清得能透过水读日期，新瓶仍悬着绿褐颗粒。此后每次签排放单前，他都先从码头放下圆盘，把深度写在那张曾经记录“两米”的旧标签上。
explanationParagraphs: Ecological resilience is a system's capacity to absorb disturbance while retaining core functions and organisation. Reinforcing feedbacks can push a system across a threshold into another persistent state; returning the pressure to its former level may then be insufficient, a path dependence known as hysteresis. Thresholds are often uncertain and context-specific, so monitoring multiple indicators and maintaining safety margins matter more than claiming an exact tipping date.
explanationParagraphsZh: 生态韧性指生态系统吸收扰动后仍维持核心功能与组织的能力。强化反馈可能把系统推过阈值，进入另一种可持续状态；此后即使压力降回旧水平，也未必沿原路恢复，这称为滞后。临界点常具不确定性且依赖情境，因此多指标监测和保留安全余量，比宣称一个精确日期更可靠。

articles.title: The Island's Most Successful Winter
articles.summary: After one warm winter supports more goats, islanders treat that number as the island's permanent limit.
articles.summaryZh: 岛民因一个温暖冬季养活了更多山羊，第二年便把这个数字当成了岛永远的上限。
storyParagraphs: Stone Island had two lush years, and the last winter was so mild that all two hundred goats survived. Many does bore twins. Wool prices were rising, and the spring buyer promised a premium if the island could offer a larger flock next year. The herding families kept nearly every kid instead of selling young animals. They carved 260 into the pen's counting board. Green slopes and full troughs seemed to prove that the island had always been able to carry more goats; only timid custom had kept the number low.

Through spring the decision looked wise. The flock grew, milk sales rose and families repaired roofs with the advance payment. By late summer, however, goats had cropped the upper meadow below four fingers and begun stripping bark from shrubs. The animals still looked strong near the trough because imported fodder hid part of the shortage. No one wrote the shrinking grass beside 260. A headcount taken after an unusually kind season had become a promise about weather and supply boats that no one had measured.

The next winter arrived early. Wind held the fodder boat offshore for nine days, and the grass already eaten short in summer could not replace itself. Strong adults crowded the sheltered feeding place; kids walked farther and lost weight. Three newborns died in one cold week. Buying emergency fodder would keep more animals alive for the spring sale, but it would not regrow roots or remove the pressure waiting behind the next delayed boat. The families opened the old count board and saw that it recorded goats, not the conditions supporting them.

They cancelled the premium contract, sold or moved sixty goats at a poor winter price and used the proceeds to feed the weakest animals. Two households lost the income they had expected for new roofs. Afterward the islanders measured grass height, rainfall, age structure, body condition and stored fodder before deciding what to retain. They rotated slopes and kept a buffer in lush years. A wetter season later raised the safe estimate; disease or drought lowered it. No single mark became the island's permanent maximum.

The warm winter's board remained beside the goat pen in the winter wind. Its highest notch read two hundred and sixty; beneath it the herders added grass height, fodder days and the date the boat failed. The next time a doe delivered twins, the family carried both kids to the board. Before writing how many they would keep, they walked uphill and pressed a ruler into the spring grass.
storyParagraphsZh: 石岛连续两年草木丰盛，最后一个冬天又暖得出奇，两百只山羊全都活了下来，许多母羊还生了双羔。羊毛正在涨价，春季买家答应，若来年能交出更大羊群，便加付溢价。牧户几乎留下全部幼羊，没有照旧卖掉，还把二百六十刻上羊圈计数板。绿色山坡和满水槽像在证明：岛上本来就养得起更多羊，只是过去的人过分胆小。
整个春天，这个决定都很划算。羊群扩大，奶量增加，各家用预付款修起屋顶。到夏末，高坡草却被啃到不足四指，山羊开始剥灌木皮。水槽旁的羊看着仍壮，因为外来草料遮住了一部分缺口。没人把逐月变短的草写到二百六十旁边。一次格外温和季节后的头数，就这样被当成对草量、天气和补给船都有效的长期承诺。
下一场冬天提前抵达，风浪让草料船在海外停了九天，夏季已经吃短的草也无法及时长回。强壮成羊占住背风喂食处，幼羊要走得更远，体重不断下降，一周里死了三只新羔。仓里每少一捆草，羊圈夜里就多一阵叫声。紧急买草或许能让更多羊活到春市，却长不回草根，也消不掉下一次误船时仍会出现的压力。牧户翻开旧计数板，才发现上面只记了羊，没有记支撑它们的条件。
岛民取消高价合同，在冬季低价卖出或转走六十只羊，用所得照顾最弱的羊。两户人家因此没拿到原定修屋的钱。此后保留多少，要先看草高、降雨、年龄结构、体况和存草天数；各坡轮牧，丰年也留余地。后来湿润季节让安全估计回升，疾病或干旱又会把它压低，再没有一道刻痕被当成石岛永久不变的最大数。
那个温暖冬季的木板仍挂在羊圈旁，海风还从木板缝里穿过。最高一道写着二百六十只，下面又添了草高、存草天数和补给船误期日期。下一次母羊生下双羔，一家人把两只幼羊都抱到木板前，却没有立刻写保留数。他们先走上坡，把木尺插进春草。
explanationParagraphs: Carrying capacity is the population size an environment can sustain over time under specified resource, habitat, climate, disease, competition and management conditions. It is dynamic rather than a fixed species number. Populations can overshoot when reproduction or subsidies temporarily mask limits, producing density-dependent losses and habitat damage. Estimation therefore uses multiple indicators and time periods, not a single headcount.
explanationParagraphsZh: 环境承载力是在给定资源、栖息地、气候、疾病、竞争和管理条件下，环境可长期维持的种群规模，并非某物种固定不变的数字。繁殖惯性或外来补给可能暂时遮住限制，使种群超调，随后出现密度相关损失和栖息地退化。因此估计需结合多项指标与多个时期，不能只看一次头数。

articles.title: After the River Lost Its Hunters
articles.summary: A reservoir removes predatory fish to satisfy anglers, and changes then travel through minnows, grazers, algae and water clarity.
articles.summaryZh: 水库为满足钓客清除捕食鱼，变化随后经过小鱼、浮游摄食者、藻类一路传到水体透明度。
storyParagraphs: Reservoir keeper Oren needed more fishing permits to repair the west dam. Anglers complained that large pike took hooked fish and left too few small silver minnows near shore. Oren paid crews to net out most adult pike before spring. The first month pleased everyone: minnow catches nearly doubled, children filled buckets at the pier, and permit sales funded new stone. Oren hung one of the pike nets above his office and wrote the higher catch beneath it.

By early summer, minnow surveys rose from about forty to ninety fish per standard haul. Stomach samples showed that many fed on large zooplankton, the small animals that grazed suspended algae. Zooplankton counts then fell. With fewer grazers removing cells, phytoplankton increased and Oren's black-and-white clarity disk disappeared at one metre instead of three. He first blamed muddy swimmers because the change had begun near the busy shore, and he restricted bathing without replacing the pike.

The water remained green after the beach closed. Light no longer reached some submerged plant beds, which thinned and released sediment more easily during wind. Night-time oxygen dropped when abundant organic matter was respired and decomposed, and two cages of stocked fish died during a hot calm spell. The sequence had crossed several feeding levels: fewer predators, more planktivorous fish, fewer grazers, more algae, less light. No organism had intended the final water colour, and not every pike, minnow or grazer ate the same prey at every age.

Before the holiday weekend, a drum of algaecide arrived with a promise of clear surface water. Oren left its seal intact. The chemical could leave decomposing biomass and would not repair the altered food web. He closed fishing for six weeks, reintroduced pike from an upstream refuge under a fisheries plan and funded buffer strips beside two drainage ditches. The closure delayed dam repairs, reduced permit income and angered anglers who had asked him to remove the predators.

Minnow numbers declined the next season, large zooplankton became more common and the disk could be seen at nearly two metres. Water did not return instantly or solely because of pike: nutrient inflow, temperature, plant recovery and weather still mattered. The keeper kept measuring all of them. In one shallow arm, pike had little effect because vegetation sheltered minnows; in open water, the response was stronger. The chain depended on species, habitat and interaction strength rather than a universal number of feeding levels.

Oren cut the old pike net into a narrow sling for the clarity disk. Each week the same cords that had lifted predators from the reservoir now lowered the black-and-white circle through green water. On the office wall, the minnow tally remained beside every depth reading.
storyParagraphsZh: 水库管理员奥伦需要多卖钓鱼证，修补西侧坝体。钓客抱怨大狗鱼会抢走上钩小鱼，使岸边银色小鱼太少。春季前，奥伦付钱让船队捕走大部分成年狗鱼。第一个月人人满意：标准小鱼捕量近乎翻倍，孩子在码头装满水桶，新增证费也换来修坝石料。奥伦把一张狗鱼网挂在办公室上方，在下面写下增长的收获。
初夏，标准拖网中的小鱼从约四十条增到九十条。胃含物样本显示，许多小鱼摄食大型浮游动物，而后者原本会取食悬浮藻类。随后浮游动物计数下降，清除藻细胞的摄食者减少，浮游植物增多。奥伦用来测透明度的黑白圆盘，从能见三米变成一米便消失。他先怪岸边游泳者搅泥，关闭浴场，却没有恢复狗鱼。
浴场关闭后，水仍是绿色。光照不到部分水下植物床，植被变稀，起风时泥沙也更容易扬起；有机物大量呼吸与分解，使平静热夜的水中氧下降，两笼养鱼随之死亡。变化越过数个摄食层次：捕食者减少，小型食浮游动物鱼增加，大型摄食者减少，藻类上升，光线下降。没有哪种生物意图制造最终水色，不同年龄的狗鱼、小鱼和浮游动物也不会永远吃同一种食物。
假日前，一桶除藻剂送到码头，桶签许诺很快还原清亮水面。奥伦没有拆封；药剂可能留下继续分解的生物量，也修补不了已经改变的食物关系。他关闭六周捕捞，按渔业方案从上游庇护区引回狗鱼，又资助两条排水沟建设缓冲带。封闭让证费减少、大坝修理延期，也激怒了那些曾要求清除捕食鱼的钓客。
下一季，小鱼数量下降，大型浮游动物增多，圆盘接近两米仍可看见。水质并非立刻恢复，也不能全归给狗鱼；养分输入、温度、植物恢复和天气仍在作用，管理员继续同时测量。一个浅水湾里，浓密植被替小鱼提供躲藏，狗鱼影响较弱；开阔水面反应更强。这条变化链取决于物种、栖息地和相互作用强度，并无通用于所有地方的层级数目。
奥伦把旧狗鱼网裁成一条窄吊带，用来系黑白圆盘。每周，曾把捕食者拉出水面的绳索都会把圆盘重新放进绿水。办公室墙上，小鱼计数始终与每一次深度读数并排保留。
explanationParagraphs: A trophic cascade occurs when a change at one feeding level indirectly alters organisms or processes at other levels, often through predator effects on consumers and their resources. Cascades may involve abundance or behaviour and can move downward or upward through food webs. Their strength depends on species, habitat, omnivory, refuges, nutrients and other forces, so a predator change should not be treated as the sole cause without evidence.
explanationParagraphsZh: 营养级联是某一摄食层的变化，经由捕食者、消费者及其资源间的间接作用，改变其他层级的生物或过程。级联可通过数量或行为发生，也可沿食物网向下或向上传递。其强度受物种、栖息地、杂食、庇护、养分等影响，因此不能缺少证据便把所有变化归给某种捕食者。

articles.title: The Forest Counted Only by Trees
articles.summary: A road project replaces every felled tree, yet the forest's routes never reconnect after construction.
articles.summaryZh: 修路工程砍一棵补一棵，完工后树木总数没变，林中的道路却再也没有接回去。
storyParagraphs: Mayor Soren needed the timber road open before the rains. The mill promised forty jobs if logs reached the river that season, and the route occupied less than three percent of the mapped forest. The town also promised to plant one roadside sapling for every felled tree. On the plan, ecologist Miri drew a red line between two temporary pools used by dusk frogs. Soren counted equal numbers in the felling and planting columns and said the forest would remain. The crew cut a twelve-metre strip, compacted gravel and finished early. Wages arrived; the replacement tally balanced.

On the first wet night, adult frogs moved from the western forest toward the eastern breeding pool. Cart wheels and the dry gravel crossing killed many; others turned along the road edge and did not reach water before dawn. Egg masses in the eastern pool fell. Soren ordered a narrow metal culvert beneath the road, a quick repair that preserved timber traffic. Cameras showed few frogs using it. Its entrance stood twenty metres from their usual route, the floor was dry and hot, and fast runoff scoured one end.

The cleared strip also created two new edges. Rows of replacement saplings stood beside it, yet sun and wind dried the moss, lights changed night conditions and invasive grass arrived on truck tyres. The young trees restored a number, not old shaded interiors or the route between pools. Dusk frogs avoided the brightest section, while an edge-tolerant lizard became more common. Counting hectares and trunks had missed configuration: one connected area and two separated patches could contain similar totals yet offer different movement, shelter and mating opportunities.

For five breeding seasons, Miri marked frogs at both pools. Recaptures across the road dropped almost to zero. The western pool occasionally dried before tadpoles transformed, and adults there could no longer readily join the eastern pool. Genetic samples began to show reduced exchange, though the populations were not yet separate species and a few crossings still occurred. The road had combined direct loss, edge change, mortality and isolation; none required the forest on either side to disappear.

The mill's widening permit lay ready for Soren's signature and promised to keep all forty jobs. He left it unsigned and ordered the crossing rebuilt first: a raised, broad underpass aligned with the wet migration route, moist soil and cover through it, less lighting and several rain-night closures. The redesign consumed the widening budget. Trucks made fewer journeys, the mill cancelled eight seasonal posts, and residents accused Miri of valuing frogs above families.

The new passage improved crossings but did not make the road vanish. Some frogs still died, edge vegetation recovered slowly, and storms sometimes blocked the underpass. Rangers cleared debris and compared camera counts rather than declaring success after construction. Where possible, the town protected an uncut strip linking other pools, because a corridor could reduce isolation but could not replace all habitat quality, width or routes lost elsewhere.

Miri kept the first planning map on the council wall. The red road still divided the green paper. At the underpass, she cut a narrow opening and stitched it with green thread, then hung the first rain-night crossing count beneath it. Beside the map, the old felling and planting columns still ended at the same number. The green thread crossed only one opening; across the rest of the sheet, the red road remained unbroken.
storyParagraphsZh: 索伦镇长必须在雨季前开通木材路。锯木厂承诺，只要当季原木能运到河边，便提供四十份工作；路线占地图森林面积不到百分之三。镇里还承诺砍一棵便在路边补种一棵。规划纸上，生态员米莉在两座黄昏蛙使用的雨池之间画出红线。索伦看见砍伐栏与补种栏数目相等，便宣布森林仍在。施工队砍出十二米宽地带，压紧碎石，提前完工；工资按时发放，树木账也正好平衡。
第一个湿夜，成年蛙从西侧森林移向东侧繁殖池。车轮和干燥碎石路杀死不少个体，另一些沿道路边缘绕行，天亮前没能抵达水面，东池卵团随之减少。索伦让人在路下装一根窄金属涵管，既快又不耽误运木。相机却很少拍到蛙进入：入口偏离旧路线二十米，管底干燥发热，一端还被急流冲刷。
清理带又制造了两条新边缘。补种幼树已经成排站着，阳光和风仍让苔藓变干，灯光改变夜间条件，入侵草也随车轮进入。幼树补回头数，却补不回老林阴湿内部和两池之间的旧路线。黄昏蛙避开亮处，一种耐边缘蜥蜴反而增加。只数公顷与树木漏掉了排列：总量相近的一整片和两块隔开的林地，提供的移动、躲藏与交配机会并不相同。
连续五个繁殖季，米莉在两座池塘标记蛙。跨路再捕数量接近于零。西池偶尔在蝌蚪完成变态前干涸，那里的成蛙又难以转入东池。遗传样本开始显示交流减少，不过两群还没有成为不同物种，少数个体也仍能穿越。道路把直接占地、边缘改变、路杀与隔离叠在一起，这些后果不需要道路两边的森林完全消失才会发生。
锯木厂的拓宽许可已经摆到索伦面前，签字便能保住四十份工作。他没有落笔，先命人重建穿越设施：抬高道路，设置与潮湿迁徙线对齐的宽通道，在里面恢复湿土与遮蔽物，减少照明，并在几个迁徙高峰雨夜封路。改建吃掉拓宽预算，卡车班次减少，锯木厂取消八个季节岗位，居民指责米莉把青蛙看得比家庭重要。
新通道增加了穿越，却没有让道路消失。仍有蛙被压死，边缘植被恢复缓慢，暴雨也会堵住入口。巡护员定期清除杂物，用相机计数比较变化，没有在竣工当天宣布成功。其他雨池之间若还能保留未砍连接带，镇里便优先保留；廊道可减轻隔离，却不能替代各处失去的全部生境质量、宽度和路线。
米莉把第一张规划图留在议事厅。红路仍把绿色纸面分成两边。她在通道位置切开窄口，用绿线缝起，又把首个雨夜的穿越数挂在下面。地图旁，旧砍伐栏与补种栏仍停在同一个数字。绿线只穿过那一道开口，红路在纸面其余部分仍连续不断。

Effects can include altered microclimate, movement barriers, mortality, reduced gene flow and weaker recolonisation, and they differ among species and landscapes. Corridors or crossings may improve connectivity but cannot automatically replace habitat area, quality, multiple routes or long-term maintenance.
